source_scope: tex/chapters/03_decompositions.tex, eq:conv_split and prop:conv_correct; supplies the convolution-chunk instance used in thm:cnn_split_correct, not the entire CNN composition theorem on its own.
semantic_findings: applyKernel is defined independently as a direct finite tensor sum over input channels and kernel taps. Its coefficient indices are output channel, input channel, tap; the stencil indices are output position and tap. Kernel coefficients and output-channel biases are shared across output positions.

finProdFinEquiv flattens channel and position with position as the fast coordinate. Both sampling and the matrix construction use the same inverse equivalence. The flattening bridge reindexes the actual input-column sum through this equivalence and proves the optional sample-selector identity.
A missing sample is exactly zero padding. The kernelMatrix entry sums all matching taps; no stencil injectivity assumption is present, and repeated taps are accumulated rather than overwritten.

The sign split is correctly performed at the kernel-parameter level before flattening. When opposite signed taps share a sample, kernelMatrix (positiveKernel K) need not be the positive part of kernelMatrix K. No such false equality is asserted. The proved subtraction identity is the correct one.
Biases are broadcast once per output position according to output channel and split with max b 0 and max (-b) 0. They are not accidentally summed once per input channel or tap.

splitKernel_eq_affineChunk identifies the literal tensor split with the actual shared affine chunk. Nonnegative outputs require nonnegative pair inputs; monotonicity, affine dependence and coordinate convexity hold globally. Recovery is proved for every real input pair, without a nonnegativity premise.

The ordinary Frechet derivative is the actual induced matrix. The split derivative has blocks A+, A-, A-, A+ in that order, through the existing preP and preN continuous linear maps, with no derivative contribution from the constant bias.

All finite dimension binders are unrestricted. Empty input-channel or tap sums vanish, absent input positions force samples to be none, and empty output spaces make the coordinate assertions correctly vacuous.
adversarial_examples: Two taps +1 and -1 at the same input position: ordinary matrix entry is 0, while both kernel-sign matrices have entry 1.
The same repeated taps with negative bias -3: the split streams are p+q and q+p+3, so the bias is correctly recovered once.
Two input channels, two positions, two taps, shared weights [1,2] and [3,4], one padded tap, and shared bias -5: direct tensor outputs are 5 and 25 under channel-major input [1,2,3,4].
Zero input channels, zero kernel taps and zero input positions each produce the zero unbiassed convolution.
Zero output channels produce the unique empty output pair.
scope_limits: The sampling stencil is an explicit mathematical parameter. The leaf does not separately formalize the arithmetic construction of a stencil from framework stride, dilation, padding, spatial-shape or tensor-layout options.
No PyTorch implementation, graph parser, converter, floating-point kernel, backward implementation or serialization is certified by these mathematical results.

Kernel-level and matrix-entry-level canonical sign parts coincide for the usual noncolliding samples, but the stronger arbitrary-stencil theorem deliberately requires only the proved difference identity.
